correctness.rationale: The biquadratic function field k(x)(sqrt(P),sqrt(Q)) is degree 4 since branch loci disjoint; its eight simple branch values yield genus5 by Riemann–Hurwitz. The affine singularity equations force y=0, P−Q=0, and P=Q nonzero at such points. The local exact square-root change y sqrt(2(P+Q)-y²) reduces equation to v²−(P−Q)²; a multiplicity-e root gives A_{2e−1}. Homogenization with quartic P4,Q4 and cubic D3 gives at (0:1:0) completed v²−u⁴ and at (1:0:0), when d<3, v²−u^{2(3−d)}; no other infinite singularities. Two smooth branches intersect at order e and sum delta=5. Independent exact symbolic quartics P=x^4+x+1, Q=P−D for all seven root partitions have squarefree coprime branch quartics (nonzero Q discriminants), supporting nonemptiness. The local proof covers unrestricted parameters; seven examples alone do not.
